correctnessFindings.assessment: The sweep identifies live OSC 8 link IDs in normal and alternate buffer cells, the active input attribute, and both saved-cursor attributes before disposing any stale link markers.

The collector runs after writes in headless terminals and through the write-parsed addon in renderer and mobile terminals. Registry growth of 1024 entries triggers a sweep; this is a sweep interval, not a limit on live links.

Guards around the private xterm registry and input handler return without collection if their shape is unavailable. Disposing markers uses xterm ownership to remove both registry indexes; the marker array is copied before mutation.

originalReview.userVisibleBeforeAfter: Live hyperlinks, saved cursor state, and existing scrollback remain available. URLs belonging only to overwritten or discarded cells can be retired. Large buffers incur a cell scan after enough registry growth.
originalReview.capacityAndDataLoss: No new scrollback or hyperlink count limit. The sweep keeps live IDs even above 1024 entries; the additional cost is periodic scanning of both buffers.

platformEvidence.assessment: The liveness calculation is shared TypeScript, and integrations cover desktop renderer, headless daemon, popout, and mobile terminal construction. Private xterm shape is package-version sensitive. Historical browser/headless controls do not prove native GPU or all-OS rendering.
platformEvidence.executedHost: Fresh shared batch: macOS darwin arm64; Node 26.6.0. PRs outside that batch have no new execution in this follow-up.

originalReview.sshAndFolderCases: Remote terminal output is parsed by the existing local renderer or execution-host headless instance. The sweep changes neither the remote wire format nor host liveness. Folder and Git workspaces share the same terminal path.

regressionCoverage.description: Published terminal-osc-link-retirement controls and the audit reproduction exercise stale versus live cells, alternate buffer, open attributes, and saved cursor state.
